what: Bootstrapping a derived quantity: the median lethal dose
title: Getting started with parametricboot
text: coefficients logistic dose-response model log-odds scale, scientifically relevant quantity may dose estimated mortality probability reaches 50%, often called LD50. female reference group model , LD50̂F=2−β̂0/β̂log⁡2(dose). \widehat{\mathrm{LD50}}_{\mathrm F} = 2^{-\widehat\beta_0/\widehat\beta_{\log_2(\mathrm{dose})}}. named statistic callback lets bootstrap track quantity directly. also provides separate estimate males including fitted `sexM` coefficient. callback calculates dose scale, log-dose scale; interval coefficients interchangeable interval nonlinear ratio. ```{r derived-ld50} ld50 <- function(model) { beta <- stats::coef(model) slope <- unname(beta[[“log2(dose)”]]) c( female_LD50 = 2^(-unname(beta[[“(Intercept)”]]) / slope), male_LD50 = 2^( -(unname(beta[[“(Intercept)”]]) + unname(beta[[“sexM”]])) / slope ) ) } ld50_boot <- pb_simulate( fit, n = 500, seed = 2025, keep_fits = FALSE, statistic = ld50 ) pb_confint(ld50_boot, type = “percentile”) pb_mc_error(ld50_boot) ``` intervals conditional fitted binomial model. Near-zero fitted slopes can create extreme LD50 values; diagnose bootstrap distribution fraction failed refits rather silently discarding observations.

what: Independent benchmark: a normal-model linear contrast
title: Getting started with parametricboot
text: Gaussian linear model, pivot formed coefficient contrast estimated standard error exact Student t distribution model assumptions. can compare bootstrap-t interval exact t interval specified contrast. ```{r derived-linear-contrast} linear <- stats::lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars) contrast <- function(model) { c(wt_plus_hp = unname(sum(stats::coef(model)[c(“wt”, “hp”)]))) } contrast_se <- function(model) { weight <- c(0, 1, 1) V <- stats::vcov(model) c(wt_plus_hp = sqrt(unname(drop(crossprod(weight, V %% weight))))) } contrast_boot <- pb_simulate( linear, n = 1000, seed = 2025, keep_fits = FALSE, statistic = contrast, statistic_se = contrast_se ) observed <- unname(contrast(linear)) half_width <- stats::qt(0.975, stats::df.residual(linear))  unname(contrast_se(linear)) exact_interval <- c(lower = observed - half_width, upper = observed + half_width) exact_interval pb_confint(contrast_boot, type = “student”) ``` bootstrap estimate subject Monte Carlo error, unlike exact normal-model pivot.
